ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the metal frame is a closed right-triangular loop composed of ab, bc, and ca, side ab is in the vertical direction on the left side, a is below, b is above, and c is at the upper right; the dashed rotation axis coincides with side ab, and angular velocity ω is marked beside it to indicate rotation about this vertical axis; the arrow of magnetic field B is vertically upward, parallel to the direction of side ab. Then reason: According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, whether there is induced current in a closed loop depends on whether the magnetic flux through the loop changes with time. Since the rotation axis ab is parallel to the direction of the magnetic field, when the triangular frame rotates about ab, the plane of the wire frame always contains the direction of magnetic field B, therefore the magnetic induction lines are always along the direction of the plane of the wire frame and do not perpendicularly pass through the area of the wire frame.
